clue.text: Turn up ends of fabric to form fringe

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the four words that follow is taken in turn

explanation.surface: A sewing instruction: fold the edges of the cloth over to make a fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like a hemming instruction, but it is the definition; 'ends of' covers all four words after it, not just 'fabric'.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is to arrive or appear, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fragrant one does for our arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters is a reordering, so the pieces before it are mixed together

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-smelling sorts out a flower display on our behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' makes the surface sound floral, but it signals that I with DOES, FOR and OUR are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Odoriferous means giving off a smell, here a pleasant one, so it matches sweet-scented.

clue.text: Below par performance, I'd heard, quick to pick up

parts.note: in golf an eagle is a hole played two strokes under par

indicators.note: heard says the word that comes before it is to be taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: I'd, a contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A golfer recalls a round that beat par and remembers being sharp-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below par' sounds like poor form, but in golf it is good: an EAGLE is two under par.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eagle-eyed spots details at once, so they are quick to pick things up visually.

clue.text: Fellow with weapon containing Argentine element in conflict

indicators.note: containing means the armed piece holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: someone with a weapon is armed
Ag is the symbol for silver, from Latin argentum, the root of Argentina's name
a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An armed man carrying a piece of silver from Argentina goes to war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine' suggests a country, but here it is the Latin argentum, silver, giving AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final great battle, so used loosely for any catastrophic conflict.

clue.text: Skill of abnormal proportions, getting around one's peers

indicators.note: getting around says the first pieces wrap themselves about the next one

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
one's read as one is gives I and IS
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, used of extra-large clothing

explanation.surface: A gifted person with outsize talent circulates among the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristos is a short informal word for aristocrats, and peers of the realm are aristocrats.

clue.text: Passionate sailor snared me-totally captivated female!

definitions.text: Passionate sailor snared me-totally captivated female!

parts.note: mad means passionately keen, as in mad about someone

indicators.note: snared means the sailor piece catches the next word within it

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: captivated means the totally piece holds the female letter captive inside it

parts.note: utterly means totally

explanation.surface: A heroine exclaims that an ardent naval man trapped her and won her heart completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the story of Puccini's opera: Cio-Cio-San is captivated by the sailor Pinkerton.
explanation.definitionFit: In Puccini's opera the title heroine is a woman entirely won over by an American naval officer.

clue.text: Close under gallery gives blessing

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the close piece comes below the gallery piece

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
a close is an end, as in the close of day

explanation.surface: The end of a show in the top gallery brings relief.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GODS is the British name for the cheapest, highest seats in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is a welcome stroke of luck, a blessing that arrives just when needed.

clue.text: Might he have bowled one for a duck?

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis ... famously finished his game of bowls before facing the Armada
a male duck has its own name, the counterpart of a duck

explanation.surface: A cricket question: could a bowler's spell have been worth a wicket for no runs?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket (a duck is a batsman out for nought), but the bowler is the Elizabethan seaman who played bowls on Plymouth Hoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake played bowls in legend, and a drake is the male of the duck.

clue.text: Students going about late joined group

indicators.note: going about means the students piece goes around the next piece

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' body
ex means late, former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Students who arrived late go about joining a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connected series or group, things linked together.

clue.text: As rambler, yearned to tour land with duke

indicators.note: to tour is to go all around, so the yearned piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: longed means yearned
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A walker, longing to cross the country with a nobleman, talks at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambler' suggests a walker in the countryside, but it means one who talks on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler in speech goes on at length, which is what long-winded describes.

clue.text: The Economist from memory backing Number Ten

indicators.note: backing means the memory word is taken in reverse

parts.note: RAM is random-access memory in a computer
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: The financial magazine recites from memory, supporting the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Economist' and 'Number Ten' (Downing Street, the British PM's home) make a political surface; the definition is a famous economist.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx wrote Das Kapital and is among history's most famous economists.

clue.text: Mum worked as librarian perhaps behind one's back

indicators.note: behind places the librarian piece after the reversed piece
back means the one's piece is read in reverse

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I and IS
a librarian lends books, so one who did so lent

explanation.surface: Mother worked quietly in a library, behind someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it is the adjective, quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum means saying nothing, as in keep mum, so it matches quiet.

clue.text: Unusually keen, when in difficulty, to make submission

indicators.note: when in means the rearranged piece is placed inside the next one

parts.note: a mess is a difficult situation

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the next word appear in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone unusually eager, once in trouble, gives in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' reads as an adjective describing someone eager, but it is the anagram fodder; 'difficulty' is the container, a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Meekness is a humble, submissive attitude, so it is a fair synonym for submission.

clue.text: Paper recalling Ruth topless among Page Three girls?

parts.note: the Sun tabloid was known for its Page Three topless pin-ups

indicators.note: among means the recalled piece sits within the girls piece

parts.note: dames is old slang for girls or women

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, means the piece is taken in reverse
topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity

explanation.surface: A tabloid hints at a woman called Ruth posing topless with the Page Three models.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid famous for Page Three glamour shots; 'topless' strips P from PITY, giving ITY, reversed to YTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday Times is a British newspaper, and a newspaper is called a paper.

clue.text: Drink with one very large group

indicators.note: with one says the drink keeps only one of its two letters for very

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A drink shared with one very large crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: BEVVY is British slang for a drink; 'with one' says only one of its two Vs stays.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a large gathering or group, originally of birds or ladies.

clue.text: Teaching graduate in fitting job on paper

indicators.note: in puts the graduate piece inside the fitting piece

parts.note: suiting means fitting, as in a role suiting someone
BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A trained teacher lands a suitable post with a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job on paper' suggests a post in writing only, but it is a newspaper job.
explanation.definitionFit: Subediting is checking and correcting copy, a job done on a newspaper.

clue.text: Did Labour benefit in time being left wing?

indicators.note: in puts the benefit piece inside the time and wing pieces

parts.note: red means left wing, socialist
avail means benefit, as in to no avail

explanation.surface: Did the Labour Party gain at a time when it was left wing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, but it is plain labour, toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To travail is to labour or toil hard, so travailed means laboured.

clue.text: Wits on reflection rank detective stories as heard

indicators.note: on reflection says the rank word is seen backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: a row is a rank, a line of people

indicators.note: as heard means the pieces before it are taken by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: DS is a detective sergeant; myths are stories

explanation.surface: Clever folk, thinking it over, rate detective fiction as hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: WOR + DS + MYTHS said aloud sounds like the answer; only the last part is respelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Wits are clever, verbally skilled people, and wordsmiths are skilled with words.

clue.text: Is a most unconventional group for a Chairman

indicators.note: unconventional suggests these letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: This is a most unusual club for its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chairman is Mao Zedong, Chairman Mao, whose followers bear his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Chairman Mao form a political group devoted to him.

clue.text: Crooked bar person serving sling and stiff short

parts.note: to shy is to throw or sling

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: stern means stiff, severe

explanation.surface: A dishonest barman serves a cocktail and a stiff, short drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is the legal profession: barristers are called to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer, a crooked member of the bar.

clue.text: Legendary hero's a bit open, with vote for resistance

indicators.note: for means the vote letter replaces the resistance letter

parts.note: a door that is ajar is a bit open
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
X is the cross a voter marks on a ballot

explanation.surface: A mythical hero is somewhat receptive, voting rather than resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is a Greek warrior of Homer's Iliad, a hero of legend.

clue.text: In general area, spotted gap

parts.note: saw means spotted
a hole is a gap

explanation.surface: Broadly speaking, in that area someone noticed an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: As a whole means considered overall, i.e. generally.

clue.text: Scotsman's appeal to be suspended from EastEnders

indicators.note: Londoners of the East End are known for dropping the H at the start of words

parts.note: a plea to be hanged would be hang us

explanation.surface: A Scot pleads to be dropped from the cast of the London soap.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End, whose Cockney speakers drop initial Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a typically Scottish man's name, so it can stand for a Scotsman.

clue.text: Long film was missing odd bits, turning up in China

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
missing odd bits means the first, third, fifth letters and so on are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An epic picture lost scenes before appearing in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China means mate from Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate; the even letters OGIMA are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, and china is British slang for a friend.

clue.text: Player given hand within two years having ability to rise?

indicators.note: within means the player piece sits inside the two years

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two of them give YY
in bridge East is one of the four players, each dealt a hand

explanation.surface: A card player dealt a hand over two years shows he can get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' suggests standing, but the definition is about dough rising with yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty dough contains yeast, which makes it rise, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bag interest — a lot!

definitions.meaning: to hold someone's attention strongly, enthral

explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a holdall, and to grip a reader is to interest them greatly.

clue.text: Feast amply after travelling light

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Eat generously once you've finished your journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like eating lightly, but it is a lamp: the miner's lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety lamp is a miner's lamp, a kind of light designed not to ignite gas.

clue.text: Note as penned by different forecaster

parts.note: so is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: penned by means the as piece is enclosed by the different piece

parts.note: other means different
say means as, for example

explanation.surface: A musician writes as someone else does, predicting things.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer foretells the future, so is a forecaster.

clue.text: Hopes to turn to this sector of industry?

indicators.note: a sector is a section, so part of the next word supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A gloomy thought about the fate of one branch of manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sector of industry' looks like an economic term, but it is the run of letters inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes are said to turn to dust when they come to nothing.
